parts.title: Hypergendered Logic
parts.explanation: Scope/front matter identifying HGL as an invented formal system for recursively structured fictional femaleness/maleness. It establishes breadth, not a standalone operator axiom.
reader_cautions: Do not treat the title as a theorem or as a real-world medical claim.

parts.title: Preface: what this document is
parts.explanation: Interpretation contract: track negation scope; separate classical logic from HGL-specific operations; and distinguish strict deduction, broader logical inference, causal deduction, causal inference, and illustrative phenotype examples.
reader_cautions: HGL is explicitly fictional formal biology; illustrative morphology is not automatically forced by the logic.

parts.title: Executive orientation
parts.explanation: Systemmap: PA tracks irreducible developmental-causal mode, IH tracks inheritance/provenance, PH tracks irreducible possession of a whole source phenotype-profile, and Γ tracks global Archstage meta-phenotype. Higher categories are typed recursive structures, not a single percentage axis; Archstage and ordinary maturation are separable.
reader_cautions: Do not conflate PA, IH, PH, Γ, or stage constancy with phenotype constancy.

parts.title: Part I — The formal vocabulary
parts.explanation: Defines the typed grammar and anti-collapse laws. PA does not distribute over conjunction; IH(Z) implies Z but possession does not prove inheritance; IH(¬Z) differs from ¬IH(Z); PH is irreducible whole-profile possession and differs from both PA and IH; Boolean equivalence inside an operator does not license operator distribution.
reader_cautions: Track expression type before simplifying; substitution inside an operator is not distribution through that operator.

parts.title: Part II — The deontic epiphany and scope of negation
parts.explanation: Uses the deontic analogy to isolate inner versus outer negation. ¬PA(φ) means the PA-state does not obtain, whereas PA(¬φ) is a positively specified developmental mode. Thus Unfemale/Unmale are not mere non-Female/non-Male states. Higher antithetical productivity comes from inheriting a structured non-state, IH(¬S), rather than negation itself creating phenotype.
reader_cautions: Do not equate ¬PA(p) with PA(¬p), or bare ¬S with IH(¬S).

parts.title: Part III — De Morgan’s laws, carefully and at multiple levels
parts.explanation: De Morgan equivalence is valid at the Boolean depth where NOT actually scopes. It may normalize Boolean content inside PA or outer Boolean combinations of HGL atoms, but it does not move NOT through PA, IH, or PH. The discipline is scope-first simplification.
reader_cautions: Do not turn ¬PA(φ) into PA(¬φ), or operator distribution into Boolean normalization.

parts.title: Part IV — First-order Suprafemale and Supramale
parts.explanation: Corrected base case: SF1=PA(x∧¬y) and SM1=PA(¬x∧y). Each is one irreducibly joint PA source. No IH, PH, UD, or FD term is constitutive at Stage 1; category typing is separate from deriving standalone PA routes.
reader_cautions: Do not decompose SF1/SM1 into two independent PA modes or import superseded Stage-1 IH/PH structure.

parts.title: Part V — Second-order Hypergendered states: inherited states plus whole-state phenotypes
parts.explanation: Stage 2 is the first multi-axis enriched state: same-side predecessor inheritance, inherited opposite non-state, positive same-side PH, explicit NOT-PH opposite exclusion, UD, two newly explicit standalone PA routes, and NOT-FD. Negating the whole state uses outer De Morgan without migrating NOT through IH/PH/PA/UD/FD.
reader_cautions: IH(¬opposite)≠¬IH(opposite); NOT PH(opposite)≠PH(¬opposite); Stage-2 standalone PA routes are not decomposition of Stage 1.
source_cautions: Part V locally contains prose that can read NOT PH(SM1) as positive possession of a non-SM1 profile, while its explicit formulas and negation expansion distinguish NOT PH(SM1) from PH(NOT SM1). This dataset records the conflict instead of silently reconciling it.

parts.title: Part VI — Third-order Suprafemale and Supramale under IH + PH
parts.explanation: Stage 3 makes source-depth explicit: the whole Stage-2 state becomes a new inheritance source and same-side phenotype-profile source. SF3/SM3 preserve structured opposite non-state inheritance, same-side PH, opposite NOT-PH exclusion, UD, and NOT-FD. Novelty is recursive provenance depth, not merely new Boolean truth values.
reader_cautions: PH(¬S)≠¬PH(S); IH(¬S)≠¬IH(S); direct provenance should not be flattened into transitive consequences.

parts.title: Part VII — General higher-order architecture
parts.explanation: Generalizes the finite SF/SM successor sector. Successors inherit same-side predecessors and structured opposite non-states, carry same-side PH and opposite NOT-PH exclusion, plus UD and NOT-FD. It defines inheritance depth and phenotype-source order, showing that recursive source depth can grow without reducing to visible-trait count.
reader_cautions: Stage number is not visible-trait count; truth-functional overlap does not erase HGL-state/provenance novelty.

parts.title: Part VIII — The three layers of inference
parts.explanation: Establishes the source’s epistemic labels. Logical deduction is forced by definitions plus classical logic; broader logical inference is structurally supported but not strictly forced; causal deduction requires an explicit causal/phenotype law; causal inference is causally motivated but leaves exact outcomes underdetermined. These labels prevent explanatory prose from being mistaken for theoremhood.
reader_cautions: Do not upgrade a possible or causally plausible phenotype into a deduction without an explicit bridge law.

parts.title: Part IX — The antithetically productive zig-zag
parts.explanation: Explains why higher recursion is positively productive rather than merely negative. Bare ¬SM_n is a non-state, but IH(¬SM_n) is a positively represented inherited structure inside SF_{n+1}; the male side mirrors this. PA-level antithesis and whole-state IH antithesis are distinct mechanisms. Boolean redundancy therefore does not imply inheritance/provenance redundancy.
reader_cautions: Do not treat IH(¬S) as merely ¬S, or infer that projected Boolean sameness makes two provenance histories identical.

parts.title: Part X — Hidden dimensions rather than arbitrary alien properties
parts.explanation: Argues that stable FemaleType/MaleType classification can coexist with increasingly deep inherited architecture. The permitted novelty is constrained by the HGL category and causal history, so the framework motivates hidden female-/male-compatible dimensions rather than arbitrary unrelated properties. Exact prediction may become harder while category classification remains stable.
reader_cautions: Hidden-dimensional possibility is not a license to invent any property; biological/category constraints remain in force.

parts.title: Part XI — Aliza’s month-by-month developmental story
parts.explanation: Illustrative developmental walkthrough separating strict HGL structure from possible phenotype realization. Aliza moves from ordinary womanhood through SF1, SF2, SF3 and deeper stages; higher months add lineage/provenance depth and may permit delayed, thresholded, suppressive, enabling, or network-level emergence. The month schedule and concrete traits are illustrative unless independently axiomatized.
reader_cautions: 'Hidden' means newly generable or structurally latent possibility, not necessarily pre-existing concealed anatomy; the month schedule is not a universal law.

parts.title: Part XII — Comparing ordinary womanhood, low Archwomanhood, and very high Archwomanhood
parts.explanation: Separates recursive Archstage depth from ordinary maturation and visible magnitude. A woman can plateau at an Archstage while puberty, maturation, aging, repair, and other ordinary biological processes continue within that stage. Low/intermediate/high Archwomanhood differ primarily in recursive architecture, provenance, and potential causal organization—not guaranteed stereotypical appearance or maturity.
reader_cautions: Archstage stagnation is not biological stasis; higher stage does not guarantee a visibly stronger phenotype.

parts.title: Part XIII — Archmanhood: the exact parallel
parts.explanation: Mirrors the Archwomanhood analysis for male-directed states. Low and higher Archmanhood deepen recursive male-side inheritance/profile architecture while ordinary man-development can continue independently of stage progression. The same distinction between stage depth, maturation, and phenotype underdetermination applies.
reader_cautions: Do not infer arrested man-development from fixed Archmale stage or assume higher stage fixes a particular morphology.

parts.title: Part XIV — Proof library
parts.explanation: Collects formal propositions separating what follows by definition/classical logic from what requires extra causal assumptions. It proves core scope, PA irreducibility, IH projection/non-converse, nested provenance depth, local finite inheritance depth, stage-typing distinctions, exact-substage coherence, stagnation≠developmental stagnation, phenotype underdetermination, and biological-domain confinement. It also labels causal-developmental claims that need explicit phenotype laws.
reader_cautions: Use this part as the theorem/audit layer; do not cite causal inferences as if they were propositions proved from HGL syntax alone.

parts.title: Part XV — Causal-developmental formalization
parts.explanation: Introduces a developmental state representation and phenotype map to show why a logical HGL state does not uniquely determine concrete anatomy/physiology. Phenotype may depend on HGL stage, inheritance provenance, profile structure, ordinary development, environment, and other biological variables. Nonlinear interactions allow emergence; female-/male-directed emergence remains biologically confined unless an explicit cross-domain bridge is added.
reader_cautions: Logical state identity is not a complete phenotype function; causal inference needs bridge assumptions.

parts.title: Part XVI — Possible phenotype spaces
parts.explanation: Catalogues illustrative Archfemale and Archmale anatomical/physiological phenotype families. These examples demonstrate how high recursive depth could widen the space of biologically directed causal organization, but they are possibility examples rather than mandatory canon anatomy. HGL alone does not force one specific morphology.
reader_cautions: Treat listed phenotypes as illustrative possibility-space members unless separately declared canonical/necessary.

parts.title: Part XVII — Worked reasoning
parts.explanation: Operational test suite. Multiple model worlds can realize the same high HGL stage differently, demonstrating phenotype underdetermination. Worked cases exercise negation scope, PA irreducibility, inheritance provenance, PH distinctions, exact stage identity, stagnation, and causal-label discipline. The section is useful for checking whether an implementation preserves types instead of flattening them.
reader_cautions: Worked examples validate reasoning patterns; they do not override the authoritative precedence rules stated by the source.

parts.title: Part XVIII — How an AI should represent and reason about HGL
parts.explanation: Implementation guidance for machine reasoning: use a typed AST; preserve distinct surface, normalized-Boolean, typed-HGL, provenance, and phenotype/causal representations; never flatten IH provenance; never invent source provenance; preserve PA irreducibility under IH; proof-trace every 'therefore'; represent high stages as DAGs; and attach epistemic labels to claims.
reader_cautions: A convenient flattened formula is not an acceptable replacement for typed/provenance structure.

parts.title: Part XIX — How a scientist inside the fictional setting should read HGL
parts.explanation: Translates the formal system into an in-universe experimental reading. x/y are HGL formal condition predicates, not an exhaustive real-world sex-development model. A scientist must experimentally distinguish state identity, PA causal attribution, IH provenance, source structure, maturity, and phenotype; intervention design can separate routes that observational phenotype alone cannot.
reader_cautions: Do not infer provenance from phenotype similarity alone; distinguish formal atoms from real-world biological completeness.

parts.title: Part XX — HGL in layman’s terms
parts.explanation: Explains Archwomanhood/Archmanhood as recursively deep biological 'grammatical history' rather than volume knobs above 100%. A state can be classified female-/male-directed while carrying increasingly deep causal and inheritance history. Provenance-sensitive biology becomes empirically substantive only when the phenotype map responds to route/history.
reader_cautions: Avoid the 'more than 100% female/male' simplification; recursive type/provenance is the intended structure.

parts.title: Part XXI — Comprehensive question-and-answer section
parts.explanation: Reader-access and validation layer consolidating the major rules: scope, SF1/SF2/SF3 structure, IH/PH distinctions, De Morgan handling, stage identity, stagnation, hierarchy, morphology underdetermination, hidden dimensions, and one-sentence system summaries. It functions as a cross-check against common misreadings rather than a replacement for the formal proofs.
reader_cautions: When an FAQ simplification appears broader than a formal definition/proof, preserve the formal source distinction and use the FAQ as orientation.
